## TL;DR

Built a phone-width navigation shell inside the existing RepoOS SPA. Below 720 CSS pixels, the shell provides Work, Search, More and Settings; More opens the app’s existing secondary routes, including configured Releases. At 720 pixels and above, the desktop sidebar remains visible and the phone bar is hidden. The implementation reuses Vue Router, the existing config navigation gates and SearchOverlay. No Capacitor host, server picker, lock screen or security boundary code changed.

## Work and rationale

The existing `MobileTabs` component was already mounted in the app, but CSS exposed it through 760 pixels and populated it with the full sidebar navigation. That mixed phone and desktop compositions in the 720–760 interval and made the bar crowded. I retained the existing component entry point but changed its content and aligned its CSS breakpoint with ADR 0011. A new `useResponsiveLayout` composable reads `matchMedia` at the 720-pixel boundary, listens for transitions, and falls back to `resize` in environments that do not implement `matchMedia`. The app shell consumes that reactive value without relying on touch capability.

The bottom bar has four persistent controls. Work and Settings are regular RouterLinks, preserving their real URLs and browser history behavior. Search signals the existing SearchBar to open its global SearchOverlay, so search does not introduce a duplicate route or search implementation. More opens a body-teleported sheet with a scrim and the destinations provided by `navFromConfig`; this retains feature gates such as Releases, Deployments, Stories and Dev. The dashboard route is named Activity within the sheet because the existing live activity feed is part of that screen and has no separate route. Context and Agents remain their existing destinations.

The sheet uses the shared overlay contract through `data-overlay-layer`, supports pointer/touch activation, moves focus into the choices, and closes on Escape while restoring focus to the More button. Navigation links close the sheet after selection. CSS accounts for the bottom safe-area inset on the tab bar and sheet. Existing viewport metadata, manifest link, standalone web-app metadata and icon delivery were already present, so they were left in place. The implementation remains in the server-served SPA and adds no runtime dependency or second build.

## Approaches tried

I first considered treating the existing bar as a list of all routes. Inspection showed it contained many destinations and did not match the four-item phone model, so I replaced the list with a direct primary bar and a More sheet. Search could have been added as its own URL route, but the app already provides a global overlay from SearchBar. Triggering that UI reuses its existing results, keyboard behavior and navigation rather than creating parallel search state.

I also initially used `matchMedia` directly. The first changed-path check exposed that jsdom tests mount the full shell without that browser API. I added a width-based resize fallback and listener cleanup; the second test run verified both existing shell tests and the new breakpoint transition test. The first complete check then identified formatter issues in the changed Vue, CSS and test files; I ran the repository formatter and repeated the whole scoped check.

## Challenges and blockers

There was no device or installed home-screen app available in this session, so I did not claim live verification in a phone browser, standalone PWA or Capacitor WebView. The same SPA composition is designed to render in each because it depends on viewport CSS width and normal web APIs, but those runtime environments still need device coverage. The scoped UI smoke and rendered contrast checks passed on the remote runner. The changed-path suite passed with 129 tests, including the new mobile layout coverage.

The existing app has no standalone Activity route. The More sheet therefore links Activity to the existing dashboard route, which contains the activity feed. No route table or history behavior was changed. PWA install assets and standalone metadata were already provided by the app, so no additional install files were necessary.

## Key learnings

The project had most prerequisites already: an SPA router, a config-derived navigation model, a reusable global search overlay, safe-area viewport metadata and PWA manifest/icon delivery. The gap was the narrow-screen composition and an aligned breakpoint, not a lack of app infrastructure. Reusing those systems preserves feature gates and route semantics while keeping the mobile shell inside the same authenticated app.

The threshold now expresses available CSS width rather than device identity. The test covers the transition on either side of 720 and confirms that 768 pixels stays on the desktop side. Browser/device-specific installation and WebView isolation remain properties to validate on actual platforms; this change did not alter the native host responsible for those boundaries.
